lines.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
Welcome back! Did you find treasure, or just three tired pairs of feet?
We are missing one final piece, Mazen. Look closely at the front desk.
Wait, look at the corner of the guest register... under the brass pen!
A small square of watercolour paper! Hand it here quickly!
The postman left that an hour ago; there is no return address.
It matches the other three perfectly. We have all four corners now.
What does the back of this fourth piece say?
Nothing! It is completely blank except for a faint blue line.
How does a blank piece of paper help us open the small sealed envelope?
Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, Nour!

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: The word 'تقريبا' (taqreeban) means 'almost'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is تقريبا.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسأل, بيسأل).

examples.trans: Ask him what his name is on the phone!
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: The word 'مازن' (مازن) means 'مازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: The word 'طرد' (Truud) means 'packages'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صارت الضهر تقريبا! خلينا نسأل مازن إذا وصل أي طرود.
examples.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
This is طرد.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Instance noun (ism marra) from رجع ('return').

examples.text: قطار الرجعة بيطلع من المحطة الساعة سبعة.
examples.trans: The return train leaves the station at seven o'clock.

examples.text: بطريق الرجعة من السوق، اشترينا نعنع أخضر.
examples.trans: On the way back from the market, we bought fresh green mint.

meanings.note: The word 'لقي' (laqeena) means 'we found'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: في نجمة صغيرة منحوتة بالخشب! لقينا الدليل التالت!
examples.trans: There is a tiny star carved into the wood! We found the third clue!
This is لقي.

meanings.note: The word 'كنز' (kanz) means 'treasure'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is كنز.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: The word 'تلات' (tlaat) means 'three'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is تلات.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: The word 'تعبان' (ta3baane) means 'tired'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أهلا برجعتكم! لقيتوا كنز، ولا بس تلات تجواز رجلين تعبانة؟
examples.trans: Welcome back! Did you find treasure, or just three tired pairs of feet?
This is تعبان.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناقصة, plural: ناقصين).

examples.trans: Tell me what is missing in the room?

examples.text: الأغراض كاملة ما فيها شي ناقص.
examples.trans: Everything is complete with nothing missing.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قطع.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Four-sided square pane of glass, tile, or ruled grid.

examples.text: أول مربع قزاز مسحناه بين السما الزرقا وراه.
examples.trans: The first glass square we wiped revealed the blue sky behind it.

examples.text: بلاط الساحة مقسم لمربعات حجر مرتبة.
examples.trans: The courtyard paving is laid out in neat stone squares.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from ماء ('water'): دهان مائي = 'water-based paint'.

examples.text: الحمد لله الدهان مائي وبيروح بالمي الدافية.
examples.trans: Thankfully the paint is water-based and comes right off with warm water.

examples.text: الدهان المائي ريحته خفيفة وبينشف خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: Water-based paint has a mild smell and dries within an hour.

meanings.note: Imperative-only verb in everyday Arabic, inflected for gender and number: هات (to a man), هاتي (to a woman), هاتوا (plural).

examples.text: هات السلة التقيلة عنك يا أستاذ مازن.
examples.trans: Give me that heavy basket for you, Mr Mazen.

examples.text: هاتي القلم الرصاص من على المكتب يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me the pencil from the desk, Nour.

meanings.note: The word 'لهون' (lahoon) means 'to here'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مربع صغير من ورق الألوان المائية! هاتيه لهون بسرعة!
examples.trans: A small square of watercolour paper! Hand it here quickly!
This is لهون.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سعاة.

examples.trans: The postman brought a thick envelope.
I handed the signature to the mail carrier.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عناوين.

examples.text: خد رقم النزل وعنواننا لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number and our address, please.
The address is written clearly on the card.

meanings.note: The word 'مرسل' (mursil) means 'sender'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ساعي البريد تركه قبل ساعة؛ ما في عنوان مرسل.
examples.trans: The postman left that an hour ago; there is no return address.
This is مرسل.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'هلق' (hallaq) means 'now'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هلق شوفوا منيح عالكرت الأول عشان نشوف شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه.
examples.trans: Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
This is هلق.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكتوبة, plural: مكتوبين).

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Adverb 'exact, completely, perfectly'.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: The word 'عدا' (3ada) means 'except'. It is a common prep in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا إشي! فاضية تماما ما عدا خط أزرق خفيف.
examples.trans: Nothing! It is completely blank except for a faint blue line.
This is عدا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطوط.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: The word 'مختوم' (el-makhtoom) means 'sealed'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كيف رح تساعدنا ورقة فاضية نفتح المغلف الصغير المختوم؟
examples.trans: How does a blank piece of paper help us open the small sealed envelope?
This is مختوم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجمع, بيجمع).

examples.trans: Today our courtyard brings a family together!
We gathered the chairs under the tree.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: The word 'اتنين' (w-tnein) means 'and two'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جمعوا الزوايا الأربعة مع بعض... ناوليني كرت واحد واتنين وتلاتة يا نور!
examples.trans: Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, Nour!
This is اتنين.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
